investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Eval Failing: POST /api/agents Returns 409 Agent Quota Exceeded (limit is 100)
investigation.summary: The AURA observability eval for remote-agent-create (and both sibling checks remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-16T15:13:35Z because POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 with the error "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval probe never received a created agent, so zero required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) were populated and all contract assertions went unverified. This is an eval-layer failure reflecting a real API-level quota enforcement condition on the production-api runtime; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so a broader production outage cannot be asserted.
investigation.rootCause: The production-api swarm backend is enforcing a hard agent quota limit of 100 for the org used by the observability probe account. When the eval runner called createAgent() at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1339, the POST /api/agents request was rejected with HTTP 409 before any agent was provisioned. Because agent creation is the first step in all three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime), all three failed with the identical 409 message, consistent with a shared upstream dependency failure. The quota condition may be caused by leaked agents from prior eval runs that were not cleaned up, by the probe org genuinely reaching the 100-agent ceiling, or by a quota enforcement change on the API side. The exact cause among these is uncertain without inspecting the current agent count and cleanup history for the probe org.

verifierContext.siblingCorrelation.likelySharedDependencyFailure: true — verifier independently flagged this as a shared dependency failure across all three checks.
possibleCauses: Agent leak from prior eval runs: the withCleanup() wrapper in the runner may have failed to delete agents created by previous probe executions, causing the probe org to accumulate agents up to the 100-agent quota ceiling. This is the highest-likelihood cause given the 409 message text 'swarm agent already exists' wrapping the quota error.

Probe org genuinely at quota: the org used by the observability probe account may have reached 100 agents through normal product usage or accumulated test agents, leaving no headroom for the eval to create a new one.

API-side quota enforcement change: the swarm backend may have lowered the per-org agent limit or begun enforcing a previously unenforced limit, causing previously passing evals to now fail. This is a hypothesis only — no API changelog or incident signal is present in the supplied evidence.

Suspect commit 7c8e040 (low confidence): this commit touched .github/workflows/aura-observability.yml and aura-observability-repair.yml among other CI files approximately 19 minutes before the eval ran. It is possible a workflow change altered cleanup behavior or probe credentials, but the commit's candidateTouchedPaths list is empty and no matched needles link it to the 409 error. This remains a low-confidence hypothesis requiring further inspection of the workflow diff.
